positions.name: PallasineChecklistAuthority
positions.frame: what establishes the Pallasine checklist as the current, mandatory onboarding standard?
positions.why: Both expressions come from the same speaker in the same breath about the same artifact: src-1 states the checklist as a universal, present-tense mandate ('Every new hire completes'), and src-2 supplies the institutional history that grounds that mandate — the checklist superseded the old wiki page last quarter. Read together, the authority-ranking framing of src-1 and the supersession fact of src-2 answer one question: why this checklist, now, is the given standard rather than one option among others. No tension — the two expressions reinforce a single institutional-legitimacy read; conviction on src-1 registers as decision-level (ratification of the rule) while src-2 is a supporting factual claim, consistent with a mandate-plus-grounding structure rather than two independent assertions.

placements.why: The content describes a mandatory internal onboarding procedure (accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift) that superseded a prior artifact — this is organizational-process content, and no strata category exists yet in this repo to hold it. Minting the top-level Organization category gives future onboarding, staffing, and process-governance content a home without forcing it under Strategy or Product.

placements.frame: Does this content describe how the organization structures, mandates, or standardizes its internal processes, roles, or personnel practices?

placements.title: Onboarding formalized into a single mandatory checklist
placements.frame: What establishes a given onboarding artifact as the current, mandatory standard, and what prior artifact or practice did it supersede?
placements.why: src-1 states the Pallasine checklist as a universal first-week mandate (accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift); src-2 grounds that mandate historically by noting it replaced the old wiki page last quarter. Together they name a subject — how onboarding practice gets formalized and superseded over time — that future envelopes about onboarding changes, checklist revisions, or new replacements will keep feeding, not a one-time fact. No existing leaf or strata (graph is empty) plausibly holds this theme, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Organization strata.
